conversations.value: Explain how careful measurement improves engineering decisions.
Careful measurement separates assumptions from observed behavior.
Summarize the role of repeatable experiments in system optimization.
Repeatable experiments make comparisons trustworthy and regressions visible.
Describe why latency percentiles matter in online services.
Percentiles expose tail behavior that averages can hide.
Explain the difference between throughput and latency.
Throughput measures completed work per time while latency measures time per request.
Why should a benchmark fix input and output lengths?
Fixed lengths remove a major source of workload variance.
What does concurrency represent in an inference service?
Concurrency is the number of requests in flight at the same time.
Why is a warmup useful before performance measurement?
Warmup absorbs one-time initialization and compilation costs.
Explain time to first token in one sentence.
Time to first token is the delay from request submission until the first streamed token arrives.
Explain time per output token in one sentence.
Time per output token measures average decode time after the first token.
Why should failed benchmark requests be reported?
Ignoring failures can make overloaded systems appear artificially fast.
What is queueing delay?
Queueing delay is time spent waiting for service capacity before execution begins.
Why record software versions with benchmark results?
Versions make results reproducible and help explain later changes.
What is an end-to-end latency measurement?
It measures total client-observed time from request start to completion.
Why run a smoke test before a large benchmark?
A smoke test catches functional and configuration errors cheaply.
Why save raw benchmark output?
Raw output preserves evidence for audits and future reanalysis.
Why monitor GPU memory during inference?
Memory monitoring reveals capacity limits and potential out-of-memory risk.
